git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Fix staging reminder false positive on -m messages

stages_all scanned every letter of a short-option cluster for the
stage flag, so the a in git commit -m"add export handler" (the
message attached to -m) was read as -a and the reminder fired.

Walk the cluster letter by letter instead. A value option (-m, -F,
-c, -C, -t) ends the cluster, and a bare one skips the next word as
its value. Optional-value options (-S, -u) also end the cluster.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

The reminder fired because `stages_all` in `src/staging.py` read the message as options. I fixed it and committed as `05244c8`.

**Cause (verified):** `shlex.split` turns `git commit -m"add export handler"` into `['git', 'commit', '-madd export handler']`. The check scanned every letter after the dash for `a`, the `-a` (stage all) flag, so the `a` in "add" matched. The same check also flagged `git commit -m -a` (where `-a` is the message) and `git commit -uall`.

**Fix:** The code now reads each short-option cluster one letter at a time.
- A value option (`-m`, `-F`, `-c`, `-C`, `-t`) ends the cluster, and the rest of the word is its value.
- A bare value option skips the next word, so `-m -a` is not read as a flag.
- Optional-value options (`-S`, `-u`) also end the cluster. I chose this from git's option rules, not from a test of git itself.

**Tests (verified):** I added regression tests to `tests/test_staging.py`. Five of the new cases failed before the fix. After it, `python3 -m unittest` runs 7 tests, all passing. Real stage-all commands like `git commit -am "x"`, `git commit -S -a -m x`, `git add -A` and `git add -v .` still trigger the reminder.

**Commit (verified):** I staged `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py` by name. The commit has the Co-Authored-By line you specified. There is no remote, so I stopped at the commit.

I left `README.md` (modified) and `notes/` (untracked) alone. They look like another session's work, per AGENTS.md.
